transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

I'm here because... well, I just can't seem to keep my mind on a task long enough to finish it anymore. Even important things. I do computer support, and... I'll start tracing a client's network problem, and ten minutes later I realize I've just been staring at the screen. I'll reread the same log entries three times and still not know what they actually say. It's... becoming a problem.
Did you have similar problems with attention or distractibility when you were a child?

Yeah, I suppose so. My mother... she actually still jokes about my old grade school report cards. Apparently they always said I was bright, but... I never stayed in my seat. I'd just blurt out answers. And I was always losing my homework, even when I'd actually done it. So... yeah.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about different things most days?
No, not really. I mean... I guess I worry about normal things, like anyone else. But I wouldn't say it's excessive.
Have you felt down or depressed most days recently?
No... I don't think so. I mean, I'm not depressed. I just... I feel fine, mostly. Just frustrated with the work stuff, I guess.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, predominantly inattentive presentation, with childhood onset of symptoms and current occupational impairment. The patient reports persistent difficulty sustaining attention, rereading material without retaining it, and becoming distracted while working. Retrospective childhood history confirms hyperactive/impulsive and inattentive symptoms (could not stay seated, blurting out answers, losing homework). Anxiety and depressive disorders were not supported by the interview.
